Starting at 09:12:35, every card processor call from payment-svc was rejected with 401 Unauthorized (invalid API key) (#204, #211, #218, #227). Successful /charge calls stop right after the reload (last OK at #200, 09:12:10). Order-service then gets 502s from payment-svc (#210, #215, #234), and the api-gateway returns 502 on POST /checkout with 9-30s latencies (#203, #212, #262). Those gateway 502s are downstream symptoms and are not cited as evidence of the cause. The only other anomaly, a slow audit_log seq-scan at 09:13:00 (#207), is unrelated: postgres has no errors and the checkout path never reaches the database. The card processor did not hang or go down (no timeouts; the earlier reset at #75 recovered on retry), so this is not an external outage. The rotated key (version 23) is the one being rejected.

The card processor had one transient connection reset at 09:04:48 that succeeded on retry, which is not the cause. A processor-side outage would show 5xx or timeouts, not a consistent 401 on the new key, so this is unlikely.

verdict.recommendedAction: Immediately fix the CARDPROC_API_KEY in payment-svc: confirm that secrets version 23 is a valid, active key at the card processor (version 22 is already revoked, so rolling back to it will not help). Push the corrected key or roll back to a known-good key, then restart or reload payment-svc. Confirm that the POST /checkout 502 rate falls and that payment-svc /charge calls return 200. Add an alert on card-processor 401s and on secret reloads followed by auth failures, and add a validation step before revoking the previous key.
